answer: A bonded vault raises the price of every fake identity: each agent must lock collateral that is slashed if it misbehaves, so spinning up thousands of Sybils means funding thousands of vaults. Like a ridge that forces climbers through one narrow pass, the stake concentrates verification at a single checkpoint, and like karst terrain that drains shallow water away, cheap throwaway accounts simply cannot pool enough locked value to cross it - the attacker pays real cost per identity while honest agents pay once.
